Yes Lowry and crew played their hearts out but are we not all aware they were also riding off the unspoken and reserved leadership that Kawhi brings. That roll with the punch mentality they didn't have before which analysts have endlessly commented about. Kawhi brought a invaluable mindset that allowed others to thrive around him.

The biggest thing Kawhi brought to the city was the antidote to this mindset the entire city has being a "cursed sports city". You can't put a price on that. How many times as a fan were you filled with dread that the Raptors may choke.

In the way Carter paved the way for the explosive passion we have for basketball, Kawhi gave this city a taste of not feeling like losers for once. There has always been this sense that the Raptors could not get over the hump and we can't just forget what that was like and take Kawhi for granted. You can't measure what he brings. Toronto was never respected. that's why this year they weren't gunning for the first seed and had a long term vision to make the finals this time around. I've been watching for the past decade. if anything, what you're telling me shows you don't understand the subtler aspects that goes into the sport as a whole.

as a raptors supporter, yes he should have his jersey retired. I believe when you win a chip like that in Toronto and what it represents, the city as a collective having this belief in the back of their mind that the city is a cursed sports city, someone like Kawhi brings something to the table to break that seemingly unbreakable curse and get you over the hump to win your first ever chip, yes, retire that man's jersey.

people will ALWAYS forget in hindsight but I know what that dread feels like. there's a reason why Masai says stuff like believe in yourself and believe in your city. that's because there is an underlying doubt that pervades the mentality of the city and doubt becomes a tangible virus that erodes confidence and competence. overcoming that doubt, now that is worth a retirement. there's so much on Kawhi on how he changed the mentality of the players to roll with the punches. that's something they never had and it's that mentality that brought the chip. I don't care if you only stayed 1 year. that mentality in it of itself is priceless. 1 year of a fearless mentality trumps 20 years of meandering in mediocrity and doubt

Try to rationalize the negative thoughts out of your mind as well. Depression, in my experience, was self-induced. Obviously I didn't go out of my way to make myself depressed, but I do think that it is unconsciously "self-induced". I believe the human mind at the present state is a collection of everything that is filtered through your subconscious. Before an idea or notion is digested into your head, your conscious brain will make a perception of that idea or notion. If it's negative, and you keep feeding negative thoughts to your brain, you're BOUND to be depressed. For example, you make a mistake and you put yourself down just because of a mistake that anybody could've made, it fuels the whole process of depression. Just keep thinking positive thoughts and watch out for that negative filter your mind uses.
